items.title: How Wall Street Took 80% Of Tech Profits
items.text: Wall Street banks just pulled off a fifty-two billion dollar heist without buying a single tech stock. While retail investors suffered as the Nasdaq dropped 3.46 percent, Goldman, JPMorgan, and Morgan Stanley captured 80 percent of equity trading revenue. How did they do it? They acted as prime brokers, charging hedge funds high interest fees to leverage AI trades. When markets pulled back and the VIX hit 19.42, retail accounts took paper losses while banks collected guaranteed financing fees. Don't let leveraged trading trap your capital. Wall Street banks just pulled off a fifty-two billion dollar heist without buying a single tech stock.

items.title: The 7.24% Borrowing Trap Crushing Markets
items.text: High borrowing rates are reshaping who makes money in this market. With 30 year mortgage rates sitting at 7.24 percent and the Fed funds rate at 3.88 percent, everyday consumers are feeling the pinch as sentiment drops to 48.1. Yet hedge funds keep borrowing billions from prime brokers to trade volatile tech equities. The S and P 500 fell 1.82 percent today, triggering margin fees that lined bank balance sheets with 52 billion dollars. While households pay high rates on debt, Wall Street extracts record fees from institutional leverage. High borrowing rates are reshaping who makes money in this market.

items.title: Why Banks Profit When Tech Stocks Crash
items.text: When the stock market turns red, big banks still collect massive paydays. Today the Nasdaq 100 plunged 3.46 percent, sending market volatility climbing to 19.42. Retail traders panicked, but Goldman, JPMorgan, and Morgan Stanley harvested record fees. By capturing 80 percent of equity trading revenue through margin lending, these three banks generated 52 billion dollars. They do not rely on tech stocks going up. They charge hedge funds interest to borrow money and fee spreads on forced liquidations. When the stock market turns red, big banks still collect massive paydays.

items.title: Coinbase Printed $719M While Trading Dropped
items.text: Coinbase just posted a 66 percent net income surge to 719 million dollars. But retail crypto trading volume was not the hero. According to CNBC, Coinbase generated 1 billion 200 million dollars in total revenue, missing Wall Street estimates of 1 billion 233 million dollars. Instead, the driver was a 39 percent price surge in bitcoin during the third quarter, which dramatically revalued the crypto portfolio held on Coinbase balance sheet. That accounting swing pushed earnings to 2 dollars and 51 cents per share, crushing analyst projections of 6 cents per share. Balance sheet revaluation can transform weak volume into record earnings. That is how Coinbase just posted a 66 percent net income surge to 719 million dollars.

items.title: Robinhood Crypto Revenue Crashed 55 Percent
items.text: Robinhood saw its crypto trading revenue collapse by 55 percent. CNBC reports retail crypto revenue fell to 120 million dollars in the third quarter as spot trading cooled. Total net income for Robinhood dropped from 556 million dollars down to 468 million dollars, sending shares down 8 percent in pre-market trading. To compensate, Robinhood expanded into prediction markets, pushing event contracts revenue up by more than 500 percent. Options revenue also rose 31 percent to 399 million dollars. Yet when retail crypto trading freezes, brokerage profits suffer deeply. That explains why Robinhood saw its crypto trading revenue collapse by 55 percent.

items.title: AI Agents Are Now Trading Crypto On Coinbase
items.text: Artificial intelligence software can now manage your crypto portfolio directly. In October, Coinbase launched Coinbase for Agents, supporting AI tools like ChatGPT and Muse to research and execute trades. This aligns with Vice President of Product Max Branzburg telling CNBC that Coinbase is building an everything exchange for tokenized stocks, derivatives, and prediction markets. Prediction markets on Coinbase already generated over 200 million dollars in annualized revenue during the third quarter, with active traders growing 60 percent from the second quarter. As retail trading volume slows down, exchange infrastructure is handing control over to automated algorithms. That is why artificial intelligence software can now manage your crypto portfolio directly.
